hook.text: Someone zips a file, then zips the zip. The second zip is the same size. Compression doesn't stack.

buildup.text: Good compression removes all redundancy. The output looks random—maximum entropy, nothing left to exploit.

discovery.text: Re-compressing adds overhead (headers, dictionaries) without removing data. File size can even grow.

twist.text: This is exactly what Shannon predicted: once you hit the entropy floor, no further compression is possible.

climax.text: The only way to shrink further is to accept loss—switch from lossless to lossy and discard perceptible data.

punchline.text: Already compressed? You're done. Entropy says stop.

quiz.question: Why doesn't compressing already-compressed data make it smaller?
options: Redundancy was already removed; the data is near maximum entropy
